skill.name: subagent-factory
skill.description: Create specialized Claude Code subagents with guided workflows, frontmatter examples, prompt patterns, and tool scoping guidance.
skill.summary: Guides users through creating focused Claude Code subagents for repeatable development tasks.
skill.author: AaronAbuUsama

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation examples or Markdown false positives, but the skill intentionally discusses user-level Claude agent paths, shell hooks, command execution examples, network endpoints, and secret-bearing environment variables. These capabilities are not clearly malicious, but they are sensitive for a community skill and require careful review before publication.

remediation.issue: User-level Claude configuration paths are recommended in several workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer project-level .claude/agents examples by default, and add clear warnings before any ~/.claude path instructions.

remediation.issue: Reference examples include shell hooks and dynamic command execution patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Replace copy-ready shell snippets with safer pseudocode or hardcoded allow-list examples that avoid user-controlled shell interpolation.

remediation.issue: Examples mention API keys, database URLs, and credentials in environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit guidance not to paste real secrets into generated agents, prompts, logs, or committed files.

text: `Review this ${language} code for:
- Security vulnerabilities
- Performance issues
- Code q

HEADER="# Generated by Claude Code
# Date: $(date)

"
claude mcp add github -s user -e GITHUB_TOKEN=your-token -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-gith
claude mcp add postgres -s user -e DATABASE_URL=your-db-url -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-p
claude mcp add my-server -s user -e API_KEY=secret -- node /path/to/server/index.js
- 5 explore agents spawn (up to 10 if more work is detected)

content.value_statement: Creating useful subagents requires clear scope, safe tool access, and strong prompts. This skill guides Claude Code users through repeatable agent design and setup.
actual_capabilities: Guides quick creation of a custom Claude Code subagent from a known task description.
Provides an interview-style workflow for users who need help defining an agent.
Explains agent frontmatter fields such as name, description, tools, and model selection.
Offers prompt patterns for code review, debugging, research, testing, and planning agents.
Describes project-level and user-level agent placement options for Claude Code.
limitations: Does not verify that a generated agent is safe for every repository or task.
Requires users to understand the permissions granted to each agent.
Includes many reference examples that may need adaptation before use.
Some workflows mention user-level Claude configuration paths that require careful handling.

use_cases.title: Create a focused review agent
use_cases.description: Define a subagent that reviews code for a specific language, framework, or quality standard.

use_cases.title: Standardize team automation
use_cases.description: Build project-level agents that help a team run the same workflows consistently.

use_cases.title: Learn Claude Code agent design
use_cases.description: Study frontmatter, tool scoping, and prompt structure before creating custom agents.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a clear task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code subagent for reviewing TypeScript pull requests. Keep the tools limited to reading files and searching the codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Design an agent from requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: User knows the problem but not the agent structure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a subagent for investigating flaky tests. Ask any needed questions, then propose the name, description, tools, and prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an existing agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve tool scope and prompt clarity.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent definition and make it safer and more focused. Reduce unnecessary tools and clarify when the agent should be used.

prompt_templates.title: Build a multi-agent workflow set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user creating several related agents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three coordinated Claude Code subagents for planning, implementation review, and test diagnosis. Define boundaries so their responsibilities do not overlap.

output_examples.input: Create an agent for database migration reviews.
output_examples.output: A proposed agent name, trigger description, restricted tool list, and a focused prompt for reviewing migration safety.

output_examples.input: I need help making an agent but I only know the goal.
output_examples.output: A short interview that clarifies task scope, expected inputs, required tools, and success criteria before drafting the agent.

output: Rewrites the prompt to avoid ambiguous authority or scope.

best_practices: Grant each subagent only the tools required for its task.
Write activation descriptions that clearly state when the agent should and should not run.
Prefer project-level agents for team workflows that should be reviewed in version control.
anti_patterns: Do not create broad agents that can edit, run commands, and manage external systems without a narrow purpose.
Do not place sensitive credentials or private project details in reusable agent prompts.
Do not use user-level agent paths when the workflow should be shared and reviewed by a team.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It helps create Claude Code subagent definition files with names, descriptions, tool scopes, and task prompts.

faq.question: Can it create agents for any task?
faq.answer: It can guide many developer tasks, but each agent should have a narrow and reviewable purpose.

faq.question: Does it install agents automatically?
faq.answer: The skill provides workflows and paths. Users should review any file changes before using a generated agent.

faq.question: How should I choose tools for an agent?
faq.answer: Start with read-only tools. Add editing or command tools only when the agent truly needs them.

faq.question: Is this useful for teams?
faq.answer: Yes. Teams can use it to standardize project-level agents that support code review, testing, and research workflows.

faq.question: What should I review before publishing an agent?
faq.answer: Review its trigger description, tool permissions, file paths, external commands, and any references to secrets or credentials.
